beats.text: Every time your model processes a long context, your H100 GPU is actually wasting 80% of its compute cycles waiting for data from VRAM.
beats.visual_focus: A high-speed data bus with a massive traffic jam at the GPU core entry point.

beats.text: Think of it like a Ferrari stuck in gridlock; the engine is powerful, but the road is too narrow to move any faster.
beats.visual_focus: A sleek sports car trapped behind a slow-moving truck on a single-lane highway.

beats.text: FlashAttention-3 breaks this by using a fused kernel that keeps data inside the SRAM buffer, performing async tile copies to hide latency entirely.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing SRAM block inside the GPU core, pulling data in parallel while the compute unit processes the previous chunk.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is solid—calling out the 80% waste on an H100 immediately caught my attention because that's a massive pain point. I liked that you didn't use 'smart folders' or 'digital brains' to explain memory. However, when you hit 'async tile copies' in Beat 3, I had to pause to think about how the memory tiling actually maps to the registers. It's a bit dense for a 60-second scroll, but at least it's technical and not fluff.
